questions.solution_html:
• Professional sociology focuses on generating academic knowledge through systematic
  • research and theory. It emphasizes objectivity, scientific methods, and scholarly
  • publication. [K] / [CO1]

questions.question: Discuss the relevance of the sociological imagination in understanding contemporary social issues like unemployment or mental health. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• The sociological imagination helps individuals link personal troubles like
  • unemployment and mental health to wider social forces. It reveals how economic change,
  • social inequality, and policy affect individual experiences. [K] / [CO1]

questions.question: Define functionalism in sociology. / [CO4] [5x2 = 10]
questions.solution_html:
• Functionalism views society as a system of interrelated parts. Each institution
  • performs functions necessary for social stability. [K] / [CO4]

questions.question: Differentiate between the perspectives of feminism and symbolic interactionism on gender roles. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Feminism views gender roles as products of power inequality and patriarchy that
  • disadvantage women. Symbolic interactionism focuses on how gender roles are created
  • and maintained through everyday interactions and meanings. While feminism seeks
  • structural change, interactionism highlights micro-level social behavior. [U] / [CO4]
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Present a case study where the feminist critique of patriarchy leads to social reform. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• A case study of women’s movements against dowry in India shows how feminist
  • critiques exposed patriarchal control and domestic violence. This resulted in legal
  • reforms like the Dowry Prohibition Act. It also increased awareness and women’s
  • resistance to exploitation. [A] / [CO4]
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Illustrate and explain the theory of Hierarchy of Sciences / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• The Theory of Hierarchy of Sciences was proposed by Auguste Comte. It arranges
  • sciences from simple to complex as mathematics, astronomy, physics, chemistry,
  • biology, and sociology. Sociology is considered the most complex and depends on the
  • previous sciences. [A] / [CO3]
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Describe the methology used by Harriet Martineau in understanidng society / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Harriet Martineau used empirical observation and moral analysis to study society. She
  • emphasized systematic data collection and unbiased interpretation. Her work focused on
  • inequalities, especially related to women and marginalized groups. [K] / [CO3]

questions.question: Inspect the contributions of the Industrial Revolution to the development of class-based societies / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• The Industrial Revolution led to the emergence of capitalist and working-class
  • divisions. It transformed agrarian societies into industrial ones and intensified social
  • inequality. Urbanization and factory systems strengthened class consciousness. [An] /

questions.question: In what ways did Zygmunt Bauman shape modern sociological discussions? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Zygmunt Bauman shaped modern sociology through his idea of ‘liquid modernity’.
  • He emphasized uncertainty, consumerism, and the instability of social identities. His
  • work connected everyday life with large-scale global changes. [U] / [CO1]

questions.question: What are the practical applications of public sociology in contemporary society? / [CO1] [5x5 = 25] Part D Essay Type Questions Each Question carries 10 marks
questions.solution_html:
• Public sociology applies sociological knowledge to address real social problems. It
  • supports public debates, policy-making, and social awareness. It bridges the gap between
  • academic sociology and community life. [U] / [CO1]

questions.question: Explain in what ways does André Béteille describe the tension between tradition and modernity in India? How do changes in marriage, family, and gender roles reflect this? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• André Béteille explains that Indian society experiences tension between tradition and
  • modernity as old customs coexist with new values. Changes in marriage include rising
  • inter-caste unions and late marriages. Families are shifting from joint to nuclear forms.
  • Women’s roles are expanding through education and employment. [U] / [CO1]
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Inspect the theory of Alienation. Do you think there is connection of this theory and the corporate life of India. Why or Why not? / [CO1, CO3] [1x10 = 10]
questions.solution_html:
• Marx’s theory of alienation explains how workers feel disconnected from their
  • labour, product, and self under capitalism. In corporate India, long working hours, job
  • insecurity, and profit-driven work often reduce worker satisfaction. Thus, alienation is
  • clearly visible in modern corporate life. [A] / [ CO3]
  • 25900959
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025
